title: More Programs Aren’t Enough: Why EduWiki Needs Stronger Infrastructure
content:
When people think about Wikimedia education work, they often think first about events: edit-a-thons, campaigns, classroom programs, contests, workshops, and training sessions. But over time, one lesson keeps becoming clearer: education work does not scale through activities alone. It scales through infrastructure.

That realization has become increasingly important for the EduWiki Hub as conversations continue around sustainability, coordination, visibility, and long-term support for Wikimedia education communities.

The Wikipedia & Education User Group is the Wikimedia Foundation’s only recognized global affiliate focused entirely on education-related Wikimedia initiatives. Its Theory of Change was designed around a central challenge: how do we help education communities grow sustainably while improving onboarding, coordination, and impact across the movement?

The answer has never been simply “run more programs.” The research behind the Theory of Change identified deeper structural needs: clearer coordination, stronger support systems, better knowledge sharing, and more reliable technical maintenance for the tools organizers depend on every day.

title: WikiGotong-Royong Malaysia Day 2026: Contributing Knowledge, Documenting Heritage
content:
Malaysia Day is more than just a date commemorating the formation of the country. It is also an opportunity to reflect on the diverse histories, cultures, languages and communities that make up Malaysia. For Wikimedia Malaysia, this spirit is expressed through WikiGotong-Royong Malaysia Day 2026, a digital editing campaign (edit-a-thon) that brings together volunteers to enrich and document knowledge about Malaysian history, heritage, culture, local languages, and figures involved in the formation of Malaysia focused on Wikipedia Project.

You may refer the event page on meta-wiki (click here)

The concept of gotong-royong, which is deeply rooted in Malaysian society, is brought into the digital space. While traditional gotong-royong involves communities coming together and working collectively, WikiGotong-Royong invites contributors to share their time, knowledge and skills to build free knowledge resources. Each edit may seem small, but when carried out collectively, these contributions can create something much greater for the benefit of the public.

title: Wiki for Minorities Welcomes Burkina Faso: Documenting Underrepresented Communities Through Free Knowledge
content:
Wiki for Minorities continues to grow across Sub-Saharan Africa, and Burkina Faso has now become an important part of this expanding movement for diversity, inclusion, and representation in the Wikimedia ecosystem. In recent years, the Wiki for Minorities Burkina Faso initiative brought together Wikimedia contributors to address the digital underrepresentation of minority and marginalized communities across the country. The initiative was designed to document, preserve, and make more visible the histories, cultures, languages, experiences, and contributions of communities that remain poorly represented online.

The campaign placed particular emphasis on people with albinism, people who are blind or visually impaired, people with disabilities, minority linguistic and cultural communities, and other groups whose stories are often missing from online knowledge resources.

title: “I am documenting Juang culture on YouTube as it’s hard to record in books” – Interview with Juang-language writer Kshetrabasi Juanga
content:
This post first appeared under a CC BY 3.0 Licence as a part of Global Voices’ August 2026 Spotlight series, “Indigenous Rights.” This series offers insight into the lives and experiences of Indigenous peoples to build connections across regions, center Indigenous experiences, and share the stories of leaders, activists, community members, and more. It has been edited for Diff.

The majority of the world’s languages are primarily spoken, not written. So, the knowledge of the speaker communities is oral, yet Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects require written citations.

The OpenSpeaks Archives is developing a process for Wikimedians to cite oral knowledge from Indigenous and other low-resourced language communities, including nearly 20 language communities from India, Nepal, and Sri Lanka. This process includes audio-visual documentation, creating technological and educational resources, and community capacity building.

title: Celebrating Wikipedia 25 in Odisha: Outreach, Education, and Lessons in Community Building
content:
Twenty-five years of Wikipedia is not just a milestone for the global Wikimedia movement; it is a celebration of every language community that keeps free knowledge alive. In Odisha, India, the Odia Wikimedians User Group marked this silver jubilee through a dynamic series of activities blending public festivals, institutional partnerships, community gatherings, and digital contributions.

From lively cultural gatherings to lecture halls and community studios, here is the story of how we celebrated Wikipedia 25–along with what worked, what we learned, and where we are heading next.

One of our core goals was to make Wikipedia visible beyond typical digital spaces by taking it directly to people in their everyday community settings.

title: The Knowledge Commons in the Age of AI: Keynote speech at WikiConference India 2026
content:
Written version of the opening keynote delivered at WikiConference India 2026 (WCI 26) by Tanveer Hasan, Open Knowledge Initiatives, India.

I want to begin by acknowledging who is in this room. We are the people who build, maintain, and govern the most remarkable knowledge infrastructure humanity has ever created. We do this work not for profit or acclaim but because of our belief in the principle of free knowledge for everyone.

Keynotes are either information-heavy or seen as inspirational talks. I am sorry to disappoint you: this one is neither. What this is, is a collaborative discussion that I am presenting on behalf of all the organisers, the programme team and my team members. I am the voice of the talk, but the thinking is truly shared and collaborative. My goal is not to inspire you. You are already inspired, and that is why the scholarship team had such a difficult job in making its decisions. My intention is to share some data, to offer a framework for thinking about our challenges, and to ask some difficult questions that I believe we, as a community, must answer together.
snippet: Written version of the opening keynote delivered at WikiConference India 2026 (WCI 26) by Tanveer Hasan, Open Knowledge Initiatives, India.

title: Looking Toward Korea from the Ruins of Nagoya Castle: A Report on the Japan-Korea Edit-a-thon in Karatsu
content:
Early September 2026, twelve contributors—including five from South Korea—arrived in Karatsu by train from Hakata for the Japan-Korea Edit-a-thon in Karatsu. It was my first time setting foot in Saga Prefecture.

First, I took a photograph of the monument in the station plaza honoring individuals who made significant contributions to the development of railways in Saga Prefecture. The monument features relief portraits of four figures, one of whom was Kotaro Oshima. Oshima was a businessman from Karatsu who dedicated himself to local development by launching various enterprises—spanning not only railways but also banking and electric power companies. I learned about him while preparing for this edit-a-thon; having long held an interest in Meiji-era entrepreneurs, I had already drafted an article about him in advance. On the day of the event, we visited the former Karatsu Bank building—where he had served as president—and then moved to Oshima’s former residence, the venue for the afternoon’s edit-a-thon, where I published the article on Kotaro Oshima.

title: From Campus to Wiki Commons: Documenting ABU Zaria Carnival 2026
content: This is a Wikimedia documentation project designed to bridge this gap by documenting the 2026 ABU Zaria Cultural Carnival and making selected photographs available on Wikimedia Commons. The project capture the people, performances, cultural displays, traditional costumes, processions, symbols, locations and other significant elements that make the carnival an important expression of cultural diversity on campus. This was created by WUGN kaduna network team of Ramatu A. Haliru (inyor4mr), Halima Waziri, Zainab Z, and Mohammed Fadil with support from Wikimedia User Group Nigeria community support fund.

title: Digitizing Tunisia’s Documentary Heritage: From the National Archives to Future GLAM Collaboration
content:
Tunis, Tunisia — A one-month Wikipedian in Residence project at the National Documentation Center of Tunisia has resulted in the digitization of more than 3,000 historical documents, opening new opportunities for the preservation, dissemination, and reuse of Tunisia’s documentary heritage through Wikimedia projects.

The residency was carried out by three Wikipedians in Residence from Wikimedia Tunisia: Mounir Touzri, Houssem Eddin Boubakri, and Naim Garboussi. The team worked in collaboration with the National Documentation Center’s Sub-department of National Archives to identify, digitize, organize, and prepare historical materials for wider public access.

A major part of the project focused on the digitization of magazines published between 1955 and 1983, together with other historical documents related to Tunisia’s history.

The main subjects represented in the digitized collection include sport, art, and cinema, as well as other aspects of Tunisia’s cultural and historical development. The materials contain photographs, articles, reports, and other documentary sources that can provide valuable information about different periods of Tunisian history.

title: Wiki Rookies: Daejeon in-person meetup
content:
From late July to early August, roads across Korea are traditionally packed with people heading off on vacation.

In early August, the Wikimedia community in Korea and neurodivergent participants also took a special kind of vacation of their own: a photowalk in Yeongwol.

Yeongwol is well known for its historic sites associated with King Danjong, as well as for the film The Man Who Lives with the King, which tells a story centered on him.

We’d like to invite you, our readers, to join us as we look back on our time there.

The day of our photowalk, August 1, fell during what was close to the peak of Korea’s summer heatwave.

Since most of our route involved outdoor activities, we first filled up on some refreshing makguksu before heading out.

The tangy flavors of Seoul-style makguksu, the rich meaty broth of Gyeongsang-style milmyeon, and the mild, delicate taste of Gangwon-style makguksu came together to create a whole new world of flavors: Yeongwol-style makguksu.

Our next stop was Cheongnyeongpo, the first place where Danjong was exiled after being demoted to the status of Nosangun.

title: Tech News 2026 – Issue 39
content:
Latest tech news from the Wikimedia technical community. Please tell other users about these changes. Not all changes will affect you. Translations are available.

Weekly highlight

  • All wikis will be read-only for a few minutes on Wednesday, 23 September 2026 at 14:00 UTC. This is for the datacenter server switchover backup tests, which happen twice a year. During the switchover, all Wikimedia website traffic is shifted from one primary data center to the backup data center to test availability and prevent service disruption even in emergencies. [1]

    • Updates for editors

  • The Growth team tested a new post-edit notice designed to encourage Temporary Account holders to register for a permanent account. The new notice replaced multiple dialogs and a simultaneous welcome notification with a single message highlighting the benefits of creating an account. The experiment increased permanent account creation from 1.94% to 3.66%, an 87% relative increase. The change will now be released to all wikis. [2]

title: Bringing Arabic Words to Wikikamus: A Workshop with KUIZM Students
content:
Watching college students who spend their days immersed in the Arabic language got me thinking: why not run a workshop to add Arabic words to Wikikamus (Malay Wiktionary), the free online dictionary?

That idea became reality on 16th September 2026, when we held a workshop for students at KUIZM. KUIZM is an Islamic studies institution which located at Batu Caves, Selangor.

Close to 30 students showed up, and together they added nearly a thousand Arabic words with Malay translations, to Wikikamus.

A big thank you to the Wikimedia Community User Group Malaysia and KUIZM for supporting the event, and to the dedicated Wikikamus volunteers who worked hard behind the scenes to make it happen.

To all the participants: welcome to Wikikamus & Wikimedia! Here’s hoping you’ll keep sharing your knowledge with the public for years to come.

title: Wiki Loves Earth 2026 in Bangladesh: 3,330 photographs, 15 winners, and one snake that changed the rules
content:
Wiki Loves Earth 2026 in Bangladesh has closed with 3,330 photographs uploaded to Wikimedia Commons. The jury has finished scoring, and we can now announce the results.

Fifteen images take the top places, and all fifteen will go forward to the international round of Wiki Loves Earth. Alongside them, we are announcing something new this year: a special mention for the best nature and wildlife photograph that could not compete for a prize.

A field of 3,330 files is more than any jury can look at properly, so the organising team ran a first round of evaluation ourselves while the competition was running. We checked entries against the contest rules, set aside duplicates and out-of-scope uploads, and narrowed the field to a shortlist of around 500 photographs.

That shortlist went to a jury of four experienced photographers and Wikimedians, who scored every image on it and produced the final ranking.
